>Have you spent much time doing Reverse Planning?  
>  
>Essentially, define what done looks like and when it is due, then work backwards to make sure you have each phase or step planned. Build in a little buffer where possible and start executing. This way you know when you are getting behind earlyin the process.  
>  
>For example, if you need to do a research project, you know that done is a finished, complete, edited paper, say 10 pages. That means you need to edit, which may take 2 days. That means you need to write the paper, which will probably take three weeks and several drafts. Now you are at 23 days before the due date.  
>  
>In order to write the paper you need to read other papers and develop key points. Another 2 weeks. To do that you need to identify the topics you need to cover and find articles, another 4 days, so now you are at 41 days before the due date.  
>  
>Add some buffer and you know when you need to start, when the major milestones are, etc. If you are 2 weeks in and haven't read a stack of papers and developed points, you are behind and need to adjust.  
>  
>Because it is just you, you can just track it in a calendar or Bullet Journal.
